title: Virtual reality education to reduce sedentary behaviour after acute stroke: protocol for a mixed-methods feasibility trial
summary:
Following a stroke, many patients are not physically active, even though physical activity helps to reduce the risk of a  further stroke. As movement behavior stabilises after discharge from hospital, support should be provided at this stage. Instead of relying solely on traditional methods of providing health information (e.g. through a conversation), virtual reality (VR) is intended to bring complex medical information to life and convey it more vividly, thereby encouraging greater physical activity.
As this is a feasibility study, the aim is to assess whether the method can be implemented in practice. As a secondary objective, the study is also provisionally examining how physical activity patterns change and how user-friendly the VR programme is. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups.
Adults who have suffered a mild stroke are enrolled in the study within 48 hours of the stroke. The intervention group receives a one-time VR session explaining what happens during a stroke, what lifestyle risk factors exist and including motivational elements. The feasibility of the study and the intervention is assessed using so-called feasibility criteria. In addition, physical activity is recorded using an accelerometer (similar to a fitness tracker) and through supplementary interviews.

interventions.name: In addition to standard care, participants of the intervention group receive a one-time, virtual reality (VR) enhanced education session. Standard care includes a consultation with a doctor. During this consultation, the pathophysiology, secondary prevention and lifestyle factors are discussed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
NIHSS 1-5
Walking independently (walking aids allowed)
<48 h after admission to stroke unit
Exclusion criteria:
NIHSS <1, > 5
Walking with supervision, support from another Person
Cognitive Impairments (according to doctor's assessment)
Insufficient language comprehension 
Medical indications requiring bedrest (except temporary)
